summary: Steel-platform lookout on private land in Crook County, Wyoming, that replaced a 1922 pine-tree lookout in 1936; access by permission; NHLR-registered January 2026.

facts.design: steel windmill tower with open platform, replacing a pine-tree lookout

access.note: Private land; the NHLR says it is not accessible to the public, and westlookouts says access is by permission only.

facts.agency: Barrick Gold Corporation (per NHLR); firelookout.com names Homestake Mining Company/Moskee Land Corporation

events.note: Homestake Mining Company used a tall pine tree as a fire lookout and named it Moskee Lookout
Steel platform replaced the pine tree; the NHLR Built field gives 1936

evidence.supports: location on private property, Crook County, Wyoming

evidence.quote: 30' steel windmill tower with open platform.

evidence.supports: owner listed as Homestake Mining Company/Moskee Land Corporation
1922 pine tree used as lookout, named Moskee Lookout
evidence.quote: In 1922, Homestake Mining Company of Lead, South Dakota utilized a tall, pine tree to use as a fire lookout and named the tree Moskee Lookout after the nearby logging camp.

evidence.supports: 1936 steel platform replaced the pine tree; pine used for firewood
evidence.quote: In 1936, the pine tree was replaced with a steel, platform and the pine tree used for firewood.

evidence.supports: platform still used occasionally to detect forest fires
evidence.quote: is still used occasionally for the detection of forest fires

evidence.supports: not accessible to the public, private land
evidence.quote: This tower is on private land and is not accessible to the public.

evidence.supports: land now owned by the Moskee Land Corporation
evidence.quote: The land is now owned by the Moskee Land Corporation.

evidence.supports: lower half of the Stumpy Point tower erected on the same ranch in 2012; 120-foot figure not tied to this lookout
evidence.quote: 2012: The lower half of the former 120-foot Stumpy Point, North Carolina Fire Tower erected on the same ranch as the Homestake tower.

corrections.why: Firelookout.com gives a 30-foot steel tower with open platform. The 120-foot (36.6 m) figure in westlookouts is tied to the Stumpy Point, North Carolina tower erected on the same ranch in 2012, not to this lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says the site is administered by Barrick Gold Corporation; firelookout.com lists Homestake Mining Company/Moskee Land Corporation and westlookouts names the Moskee Land Corporation as owner. The sources do not explain how these relate, so the story reports both.
NHLR gives 5,918 ft (1,804 m); firelookout.com gives 5835 ft. Elevation is not a schema fact key, so it is left out of facts and the story.

notes_for_editor: Record was thin: the NHLR page is the only substantive source, and the other two are short. No staffing, fire or current-condition source was found. The brief's height_m 36.6 (120 ft) traces to the Stumpy Point, NC tower on the same ranch (westlookouts), so it is corrected to 30 ft from firelookout.com. Agency conflict is left unresolved. Two leads were not used: a Deadwood history Facebook post (search snippet only, page did not load) says the Moskee Fire burned more than 7,000 acres in 1936; and ghosttowns.com's Moskee page gives 1921 for Homestake's involvement, not 1922. Access is set to permission from both NHLR and westlookouts. No photos added: the NHLR credits Dixie Boyle but gives no license.
